name: Interpretive Selection (Bistability) Circuit
short_description: Competes between two interpretive frameworks by accumulating evidence for each, weighted by prior biases, to achieve perceptual bistability and interpretation switching.

components.name: EVIDENCE_EVALUATOR_A
components.description: Accumulates evidence supporting interpretation A from sensory signals

components.name: EVIDENCE_EVALUATOR_B
components.description: Accumulates evidence supporting interpretation B from sensory signals

components.name: PRIOR_BIAS_INTEGRATOR
components.description: Adjusts evidence thresholds based on learned prior biases and expectancies

components.name: MUTUAL_INHIBITION_SELECT
components.description: Implements mutual inhibition dynamics allowing bistable switching between interpretations

key_references: Leopold, D. A., & Logothetis, N. K. (1999). Multistable phenomena: Changing views in perception. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 3(7), 254–264.
Hohwy, J., Roepstorff, A., & Friston, K. (2008). Predictive coding explains binocular rivalry: An active inference account. Neuron, 72(1), 142–154.
design_implications: Ambiguous visual designs can create dynamic perceptual experiences; use bistable patterns strategically in art, signage, or wayfinding to engage interpretive processing
Prior beliefs bias perception; culturally grounded design symbols may be ambiguous across groups; validate interpretive clarity with diverse audiences
